title: What Would Removing This Corruption Change? Failure Attribution for Vision-Language-Action Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.27277v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are sensitive to visual corruptions, but knowing that a corruption is typically harmful does not establish whether removing it would benefit the current episode. Furthermore, when several corruptions co-occur, deciding what to correct requires understanding which ones contribute to failure risk and how much their removal would help. We define this problem as failure attribution. Detecting corruption presence alone cannot answer this question, as corruptions can be present but relatively harmless, while directly measuring removal benefits requires costly paired policy rollouts with and without the corruption present. translated_title: 移除此损坏会带来什么改变？面向视觉-语言-动作模型的失败归因
translated_abstract: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型对视觉损坏十分敏感，但知道某种损坏通常有害，并不能确定移除它是否会对当前回合有益。此外，当多个损坏同时出现时，决定应该纠正什么，需要理解哪些损坏导致了失败风险以及移除它们能带来多大帮助。我们将这一问题定义为“失败归因”。仅检测损坏的存在无法回答这个问题，因为损坏可能存在却相对无害；而直接测量移除收益则需要昂贵的成对策略回放（即分别在有损坏和无损坏情况下运行）。为解决这一问题，我们引入了一种分解式风险模型，它学习场景与损坏的独立表示，使我们能够通过潜在干预，仅凭当前图像和任务指令来估计移除收益，而无需成对的干净图像或额外的反事实回放。
tldr: 该论文提出了“失败归因”这一新问题，并引入分解式风险模型，通过潜在干预仅凭当前图像和任务指令即可估计移除视觉损坏的收益，无需成对干净图像或昂贵的反事实策略回放。
en_tdlr: This paper defines the new problem of "failure attribution" and introduces a factorized risk model that estimates corruption removal benefits via latent intervention from the current image and task instruction, without requiring paired clean images or costly counterfactual policy rollouts.
